# Kethra: controls and how to play

## Purpose
A deep-space role-playing game where you progress by solving puzzles, reading a lost
civilisation's light and talking to people, never by fighting. It was built for the TSA Video Game
Design theme: a deep-space RPG whose progression is puzzle-solving, with character stats, levels
and branching dialogue but no combat.

## Description
Your survey ship, the Wren, went dark past the edge of the charts after a flash of white light.
You wake up alone on emergency power. To get home you repair the ship, visit the worlds of an
uncharted system, and work out what the white sky is: a signal left behind by a vanished people
called the Kindling. Rated E: the only dangers are darkness, cold and distance.

## Target audience
Players aged 10 and up who like exploration and puzzle games. No fast reflexes are needed; every
puzzle can be retried at once.

## Controls
These are the same keys, in the same words, as the Controls screen on the title screen and in the
pause menu.

| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Look around | `Mouse` |
| Turn left (no mouse needed) | `←` |
| Turn right (no mouse needed) | `→` |
| Move forward | `W` `↑` |
| Move back | `S` `↓` |
| Step left | `A` |
| Step right | `D` |
| Sprint (hold) | `Shift` |
| Jump | `Space` |
| Crouch (hold) | `C` `Ctrl` |
| Interact, talk, read | `E` |
| Character sheet | `Tab` |
| Settings | `O` |
| Pause menu, close a panel | `Esc` |
| Skip a cinematic | `Space` `Enter` `Click` |

- **Look around:** Click the game first to capture the mouse.
- **Interact, talk, read:** When a prompt appears at the centre of the screen.

Numbers `1`–`9` pick a dialogue option or a colour in the Rite puzzle. Buttons in every menu work
with the mouse, or with `Tab` and `Enter`.

## How to play
- **Level 1, the Wren.** A short tutorial teaches looking, moving, the character sheet and the
  console. Booting navigation shows the system; then plot a course to Kethra (distance, days at
  cruise speed, reserve fuel cells).
- **Level 2, Kethra.** Talk to the Aiveth, Warden Corvenna and Fen. Read three inscriptions on the
  terraces, close the lantern bloom so the Wickmoth guardian settles, then sing the Rite of Three
  Breaths in the true order at the call-stone. The Heart wakes and gives you resonant crystal.
- **Back on the Wren.** At the repair station (right of the airlock), use the crystal to repair
  navigation and the Deep Scanner. The scanner finds a ring of ships at Vessek.
- **Level 3, Vessek Anchorage.** Meet Dace and Harbormaster Varro. A white-sky pulse knocks out the
  ring's power; in the breaker gallery, bring the heaters and air scrubbers back without
  overloading a 6-unit bus before the hydroponics bay freezes. If it freezes, you get another try at
  once. Read the ledger, talk to Varro, and take the conduit alloy home.
- **The ending.** Repair long-range comms on the Wren and transmit the ledger.

**Stats.** Six skills (insight, archaeology, engineering, traversal, persuasion, perception) grow
when you use them, and each new level gives a point to spend on the character sheet (`Tab`).
Higher skills open extra dialogue options, reveal hints and open shortcuts; every puzzle can still
be solved without them.

**Pausing.** `Esc` opens the pause menu: resume, settings, controls, restart the current level,
or save and quit to the title. Settings has volume (master, music, effects), graphics quality,
reduced motion, text size and mouse sensitivity.

**Saving.** The game saves by itself at every milestone; Continue on the title screen picks up
where you left off.

**Playing without a mouse.** The arrow keys turn and move, `E` interacts, number keys answer
dialogue, and `Tab`/`Enter` work every menu.
